caption:
Mr Turtle swapped sandals for stiff new work shoes, and now his heel throbs by home time.

A firm or high heel counter can press on the back of the heel and the base of the Achilles, especially in new shoes or after switching from sandals.

What often helps: shoes with a softer or lower back for a while, padding around the sore spot and a small heel lift. Deep calf stretches off a step can squeeze the area, so flat-ground calf raises built up over a few weeks are usually a better start.

A growing lump, redness and heat, or pain that changes how you walk is worth an assessment. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🐢
